paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God asked His people to look at where their time and effort were going. They said, 'The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD,' while they lived in paneled houses (Haggai 1:2, 4). I think a lot of us know that voice. It's the one that says later, and later never shows up.

Then God says it twice: "Consider carefully your ways" (Haggai 1:5, 7). Notice what He points to: they planted much and harvested little, and their wages went into "a bag pierced through" (Haggai 1:6). God says why: His house still lay in ruins while each of them was busy with his own house (Haggai 1:9). When God's things come last, even good work can come up empty, and God wants us to see that.

So what does a baker do with this? Stop and look at what you're busy with, and ask where God sits on that list. He wants His house built "so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified" (Haggai 1:8). Let God come first, friend, and let the rest of your day line up behind Him, because this story isn't over.
